content:
# Clock-domain crossings and resets

A signal that crosses between two unrelated clocks can be sampled while it changes (metastability). These are the standard
structures that make that safe, and what each is for.

## Two-flop synchronizer single-bit level crossing
For one slowly changing bit: two flip-flops in series in the receiving domain, nothing but wires between them, and no logic
in front of the first flop that could glitch. It is safe for a level that stays stable for at least two receiving-clock
periods. It is not safe for a pulse that may be shorter than that, or for several bits that must change together.

## Pulse synchronizer single-cycle event crossing
To move a one-cycle event: toggle a flip-flop in the source domain, synchronize the toggle with a two-flop synchronizer, then
detect the edge (XOR of the synchronized bit and its delayed copy) in the receiving domain. The source must not produce
another event until the previous one has been seen.

## Gray code multi-bit counter pointer crossing
A multi-bit value crossing as plain binary can be sampled mid-change with several bits wrong. A Gray-coded value changes one
bit per step, so a sampled value is either the old or the new one. Convert binary to Gray (`b ^ (b >> 1)`) before the
crossing and synchronize each bit; this is how asynchronous FIFO pointers cross.

## Handshake crossing multi-bit data
Hold the data stable, raise a request that is synchronized into the other domain, capture the data there, then send an
acknowledge back through a synchronizer. The data bus itself is not synchronized; it is stable while the request is seen.

## Reset synchronizer asynchronous assert synchronous release
Assert reset asynchronously, release it synchronously. Two flip-flops in the domain, both reset to the active level, with
the second flop's output as that domain's reset: the release is aligned to the clock and no register leaves reset on a clock
edge that is too close to the release.

## Reset rules every register and every domain
Each clock domain has its own reset release. Reset all control state (FSM state, valid bits, counters that gate behaviour).
Unreset data registers can power up as any value, so never let them reach an output before they have been written.

## What a check can and cannot show
SiliconForge has no clock-domain-crossing analysis yet, so nothing here is checked automatically. A structural tool could
find a path between two clock domains that has no synchronizer; whether a given synchronizer structure is correct for the
protocol is a design question that needs simulation with different clock ratios and, for important crossings, formal
properties. Keep designs for this tool single-clock unless the specification requires otherwise.
name: cdc_and_resets

content:
# Writing cocotb testbenches

cocotb drives a simulator from Python. These are the patterns that make tests correct and repeatable, written for cocotb 2.

## Test structure and clock
A test is an `async def` decorated with `@cocotb.test()`. Start the clock first, then reset, then stimulus:

    import cocotb
    from cocotb.clock import Clock
    from cocotb.triggers import RisingEdge

    @cocotb.test()
    async def counts_up(dut):
        cocotb.start_soon(Clock(dut.clk, 10, unit="ns").start())
        dut.rst_n.value = 0
        for _ in range(3):
            await RisingEdge(dut.clk)
        dut.rst_n.value = 1

`start_soon` runs the clock in the background. Release reset on a clock edge, never at time zero.

## Reading signals right after a clock edge
After `await RisingEdge(dut.clk)` a signal still shows its value from before the edge, because the design has not updated yet.
To read what the edge produced, wait a little more: `await ReadOnly()` for a read at the end of the time step, or `await
FallingEdge(dut.clk)` and sample there. Drive inputs after the edge and sample outputs on the falling edge, and a test
behaves the same in RTL and in gate-level simulation.

## Driving and comparing values
Assign with `.value = 5`; read with `int(dut.q.value)` or `dut.q.value.to_unsigned()`. A value with `x` or `z` bits raises
when converted to an integer: that is a useful failure, it means something was read before it was written. Compare with
`assert int(dut.q.value) == expected, f"q={int(dut.q.value)} expected {expected} at cycle {n}"` so a failure says where.

## Check against a model not against the design
Write the expected behaviour as a few lines of Python and compare cycle by cycle. A test that recomputes the answer with the
same logic as the RTL passes when both are wrong. For protocols, decode the pins independently and compare the decoded bytes.

## Randomness and repeatability
Use `random` seeded from the `RANDOM_SEED` environment variable the runner provides, and print the seed on failure. Constrain
the stimulus (legal addresses, legal opcodes) so that failures are about the design, not about an illegal input.

## Coverage of the interesting cases
Cover reset in the middle of operation, back-to-back operations, the first and last value of every counter, full and empty for
queues, and simultaneous read and write. A test suite that only checks the happy path can pass a design with a broken edge case.

## Failing on purpose
To check that a test can fail, change the RTL (invert one condition) and confirm the test goes red. Mutation testing does
this systematically: tests that do not notice a planted bug are not testing that logic.
name: cocotb_testbenches

content:
# Handshakes, FIFOs and AXI-Lite

Ready/valid interfaces and queues are where most small digital blocks go wrong. These are the rules the common protocols
follow.

## Valid ready handshake rules
A transfer happens on a clock edge where `valid` and `ready` are both high. The source must not wait for `ready` before it
raises `valid`, and once `valid` is high it stays high, with the data unchanged, until the transfer happens. The sink may
raise or drop `ready` at any time. Never make `valid` depend combinationally on `ready` of the same interface, and do not
build a combinational path from an input `ready` to an output `ready` across a block without a register in between.

## Synchronous FIFO pointers full and empty
Use a read pointer and a write pointer that are one bit wider than the address. The FIFO is empty when the pointers are equal
and full when they differ only in the top bit. Write when `wr_en && !full`, read when `rd_en && !empty`, and ignore the
request otherwise. Registering the full and empty flags instead of computing them from the pointers each cycle shortens the
critical path, at the cost of getting the update logic exactly right.

## FIFO data output first word fall through
In a first-word-fall-through FIFO the output shows the oldest entry whenever it is not empty, and a read removes it. In a
standard FIFO the data appears one cycle after the read request. State which one the specification asks for and test the
cycle after a read.

## Skid buffer break a ready path
To register the `ready` path without losing throughput, add a second one-entry buffer that takes the word that arrives while
the downstream stage has just stalled. It lets `ready` be a registered signal while the interface still accepts one word per
cycle.

## AXI-Lite five channels
AXI-Lite has write address (AW), write data (W), write response (B), read address (AR) and read data (R). Each channel has its
own `valid`/`ready` pair and follows the handshake rules above independently. A write is complete when the response (B) has
been accepted. Accept AW and W in either order. A read returns exactly one R beat for each AR. All registers are 32 bits and
accesses are single-beat.

## Counters at full throughput
A block that must accept one word per cycle cannot hold `ready` low for a bubble between words. Check the throughput
requirement against the structure before choosing a multi-cycle FSM.
name: handshake_and_fifo

content:
# Icarus Verilog compile errors and how to fix them

Icarus Verilog (`iverilog -g2012`) is the simulator behind the cocotb tests and the evaluations. Its messages are terse; these
are the ones models hit most often and what each really means.

## is not a valid l-value for a procedural assignment
A signal is assigned inside an `always` or `initial` block but is declared as a net: an `output` port with no type (which is a
`wire`), or a `wire`. Declare it as a variable instead: `output reg out` in Verilog-2001 or `output logic out` in
SystemVerilog. Signals driven with `assign` stay `wire`; signals driven inside `always` blocks must be `reg` or `logic`.

## has already been declared in this scope
The same name is declared twice, most often a port that is declared again inside the body (`output out;` and then `reg out;`).
Declare it once. If a port needs to be a variable, give it the type in the port list (`output reg out`) and delete the second
declaration.

## Declarations must precede statements
A variable is declared after a statement in a block. Move every declaration to the top of the `begin ... end` block or to
module scope. A variable with an initializer (`logic x = 0;`) inside a block also needs `automatic` or must move to module
scope.

## can not select part of scalar
A bit or range select (`x[3:0]`, `x[2]`) is applied to a signal declared without a width, so it is one bit wide. Declare the
width where the signal is declared: `input [7:0] x`, not `input x`.

## Can not assign non-array identifier to array
An unpacked array is being assigned from a plain vector, or the reverse. Use a packed vector (`logic [7:0] x`) when you want one
number, or index the array element by element.

## Unknown module type
The design instantiates a module that is not in the file: a gate, a helper or a sub-block that the task did not provide. Define
the helper in the same file, or replace the instance with the expression it stands for. Do not rely on `include` of a file that
does not exist.

## Enumeration name has an inferred value that overflowed
An enumeration has more names than its declared width can number. Widen the type (`enum logic [2:0]`), or let the tool choose
the width by writing `enum {A, B, C}`.

## Unbased SystemVerilog literal cannot have a size
A literal such as `4'1` was written. The unsized fill literals are `'0`, `'1`, `'x` and `'z` with no size; for a sized value
write all the bits (`4'b1111`) or use a replication (`{4{1'b1}}`).

## syntax error I give up
The parser lost track after an earlier error, usually a missing `;`, an unmatched `end`, or a Markdown fence left in the file.
Fix the first error that was reported; later ones are often consequences.

## timescale warnings can be ignored
A warning that a timescale is inherited from another file is not an error. Do not add `timescale` directives to fix it.
name: iverilog_errors

content:
# LibreLane flow variables and what moving them does

These are the variables the optimizer and the project flow set most often, with the direction each pushes the result. The
effects are tendencies on small digital blocks with the open sky130 flow, not guarantees; measure on your design.

## CLOCK_PERIOD target clock period
The period in nanoseconds that timing is closed against. A shorter period makes synthesis and the timing repair work harder
and can raise area and power; a longer one relaxes timing. If setup slack is negative after a clean run, the honest options
are a longer period, fewer logic levels in the RTL, or a more delay-oriented synthesis strategy.

## FP_CORE_UTIL core utilization percent
The share of the core area that standard cells occupy. Higher utilization gives a smaller die and shorter wires but less room
for the router and the repair buffers, so congestion, DRC violations and slew or capacitance violations become more likely.
Typical starting values are 40 to 50 percent for the sky130 flow; lower it when routing fails or electrical limits are
violated.

## PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT global placement density
How tightly the placer packs cells locally, in percent. It should sit above the core utilization by a margin. Too high
produces congested regions; too low spreads cells and lengthens wires. Moving it together with FP_CORE_UTIL is more useful
than moving either alone.

## GRT_ADJUSTMENT global routing capacity adjustment
A fraction (0 to 1) by which the global router reduces the routing capacity it believes each region has. A larger value
makes it avoid congestion earlier and leaves detail-routing slack, at the price of longer routes. Raise it when detailed
routing reports many violations; lower it when wires are longer than they need to be.

## SYNTH_STRATEGY synthesis script
Selects the logic optimization script in synthesis. The AREA strategies (`AREA 0` to `AREA 3`) favour a smaller netlist,
the DELAY strategies (`DELAY 0` to `DELAY 4`) favour a shorter critical path and usually a larger one. Try a DELAY strategy
when setup slack is the problem and an AREA strategy when area is.

## Reading a failed signoff
Setup violations: relax CLOCK_PERIOD or use a DELAY strategy. Hold violations: normally repaired by the flow; if they remain,
look at the clock skew rather than the logic. DRC after routing: lower FP_CORE_UTIL and PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT, or raise
GRT_ADJUSTMENT. Max slew, capacitance or fanout violations: lower utilization and let the repair steps insert buffers; very
high fanout nets in the RTL (a reset or enable driving hundreds of flops) are the usual cause and are worth restructuring.

## Variables must exist
A variable that LibreLane does not know is an error or is silently ignored depending on the version. Use only the variables
named in the PDK configuration's allowlist; do not invent names such as `FP_UTILIZATION` or `SYNTH_OPT_LEVEL`.
name: librelane_knobs

# OpenROAD / OpenSTA Verified Tcl Recipes
- **Floorplan**: `initialize_floorplan -utilization <pct> -aspect_ratio 1.0 -core_space 4.0 -site unithd`
- **Placement**: `global_placement -density <0.4..0.85> -routability_driven -timing_driven` followed by `detailed_placement`.
- **CTS & Timing Repair**: `clock_tree_synthesis`, `repair_clock_nets`, `repair_timing -setup -hold`.
- **Routing**: `set_global_routing_layer_adjustment met1-met5 <adj>`, `global_route -congestion_iterations 50`, `detailed_route`.
- **Telemetry**: `report_wns`, `report_tns`, `report_design_area`, `report_power`.
- **Forbidden**: Do NOT emit commercial-only commands (`compile_ultra`, `place_opt_design`, `opt_design`).
name: openroad_tcl

content:
# SDC timing constraints, the essentials

SDC (Synopsys Design Constraints) is the language every STA tool, OpenSTA included, reads. Times are in nanoseconds in the
flows used here. Without constraints, timing analysis has nothing to check.

## create_clock defining the clock
`create_clock -name clk -period 10.0 [get_ports clk]` declares a 100 MHz clock on the port `clk`. Every flip-flop in the
design is timed against it. The period in the project (`clock.period_ns`) and the SDC must agree.

## set_input_delay set_output_delay port timing
`set_input_delay -clock clk 2.0 [get_ports data_in]` says the input arrives 2 ns after the clock edge, so the logic behind it
has `period - 2.0` ns. `set_output_delay -clock clk 2.0 [get_ports data_out]` reserves 2 ns outside the chip. Use
`-max` and `-min` when the early and late arrival differ. Do not apply an input delay to the clock port itself.

## set_clock_uncertainty margin for jitter and skew
`set_clock_uncertainty 0.25 [get_clocks clk]` subtracts a margin from every setup check so that the design is not closed with
zero spare time. Typical values are a few percent of the period for a pre-layout run.

## set_false_path paths that never matter
`set_false_path -from [get_ports rst_n]` removes paths that cannot be exercised in operation, such as an asynchronous reset
input or a static configuration register. Use it for a reason you can state; each false path hides a violation from the report.

## set_multicycle_path paths allowed more than one cycle
`set_multicycle_path 2 -setup -from [get_pins a/Q] -to [get_pins b/D]` allows two cycles, and the hold relationship must be
moved with `set_multicycle_path 1 -hold` on the same path. The RTL must really hold the data for two cycles.

## set_driving_cell set_load realistic port conditions
`set_driving_cell -lib_cell sky130_fd_sc_hd__buf_2 [all_inputs]` and `set_load 0.05 [all_outputs]` give the ports a realistic
drive and load so that slew and delay at the boundary are not optimistic.

## What the flow generates for you
If a project gives no SDC file, the flow constrains the clock from `CLOCK_PORT` and `CLOCK_PERIOD` and applies its default input
and output delays. A hand-written SDC replaces that default, so it must include the clock definition itself.
name: sdc_basics

# Sky130A PDK Physical & Synthesis Rules
- **Node**: SkyWater 130nm (`sky130A`), standard cell library `sky130_fd_sc_hd`, nominal 1.8V.
- **Clock Budget**: Practical single-cycle logic depth at 100 MHz (`CLOCK_PERIOD: 10.0 ns`) is ~12–15 FO4 stages; avoid deep combinational multipliers without pipelining.
- **Allowed Cells**: All standard cells must start with `sky130_fd_sc_hd__` (e.g., `sky130_fd_sc_hd__clkbuf_4`, `sky130_fd_sc_hd__dfxtp_1`).
- **Metal Stack**: `li1`, `met1`–`met5`. Place horizontal pins on `met3`, vertical pins on `met2`.
- **Utilization**: Start `FP_CORE_UTIL` at 40–50% and `PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT` at 55–65% to avoid Sky130 routing congestion on `met1`/`met2`.
name: sky130_pdk

content:
# Synthesizable SystemVerilog idioms

Patterns that synthesize to the hardware you intend, and that Icarus Verilog, Verilator and Yosys all accept. Write
Verilog-2001-compatible SystemVerilog: `logic`, `always_ff` and `always_comb` are fine; classes, interfaces and dynamic
arrays are not.

## Sequential logic always_ff register template
One clocked block per group of registers, non-blocking assignments only, reset first:

    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
      if (!rst_n) q <= '0;
      else if (en) q <= d;
    end

Every register is assigned in exactly one block. An enable is an `if`, not a mux written by hand.

## Combinational logic always_comb default assignment
Give every signal a value at the top of the block, then override it. This prevents inferred latches:

    always_comb begin
      y = 1'b0;
      if (sel) y = a;
    end

Use blocking `=` in this block. Declare any temporary (`next_state`) at module scope before the block.

## Reset style asynchronous assert synchronous release
Use the reset polarity and style named in the design contract. For an active-low asynchronous reset the sensitivity list is
`posedge clk or negedge rst_n` and the first `if` tests `!rst_n`. Reset every register that has architectural meaning;
registers that are always written before they are read need no reset.

## Finite state machine template
Declare the state type once, keep the next-state logic combinational and the state register sequential:

    typedef enum logic [1:0] {IDLE, RUN, DONE} state_t;
    state_t state, next_state;
    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n)
      if (!rst_n) state <= IDLE; else state <= next_state;
    always_comb begin
      next_state = state;
      case (state)
        IDLE: if (start) next_state = RUN;
        RUN:  if (finish) next_state = DONE;
        DONE: next_state = IDLE;
        default: next_state = IDLE;
      endcase
    end

Outputs are decoded from `state` in a separate `always_comb` with a default value.

## Counters wraparound and terminal count
A counter that wraps at N counts to N-1 and resets, not to N: `if (cnt == N-1) cnt <= '0; else cnt <= cnt + 1'b1;`. The width
must hold N-1. Compare with `==` for a terminal count; use `>=` only when the count can skip values.

## Widths signed and unsigned arithmetic
Size every literal. Addition and subtraction keep the width of the widest operand, so capture a carry by widening first:
`{1'b0, a} + {1'b0, b}`. Mixing signed and unsigned operands in one expression makes the whole expression unsigned; declare
signals `signed` consistently or cast with `$signed()`.

## What not to write in synthesizable RTL
No `#delay`, no `initial` blocks (use reset), no `$display` or `$finish`, no `force`/`release`, no tri-state internal buses,
no `casex` (use `casez` with `?` or full `case`), no multiple drivers on one signal, no combinational loops.

## Ports exactly as in the contract
The module name, port names, directions and widths must match the design contract exactly. Do not add, rename or re-width a
port to make an internal problem easier; fix the internals.
name: sv_synthesizable_idioms

content:
# Formal verification with SymbiYosys: patterns and anti-vacuity

SymbiYosys (`sby`) runs three kinds of task against a design: `bmc` (bounded model check: no property fails within N cycles
of reset), `prove` (k-induction: the property holds for all time), and `cover` (a witness trace exists for a condition).

## Typed property IR you never write SVA yourself
In SiliconForge you emit typed property objects (reset value, invariant, handshake stability, mutual exclusion, combinational
equivalence, latency bound, cover reachability). The compiler turns them into SymbiYosys source and adds the clocking, the
reset handling and the history register that `$past` needs. So a property contains only plain Verilog expressions over the
contract ports: no `cover property`, no `assert property`, no `@(posedge clk)`, no `|->`, no `##`, no `$past`, and no helper
signals such as `f_past_valid`. A property that mentions a name outside the port list is rejected before it is run.

## Anti-vacuity pair every assert with a cover
A proof can hold only because its condition can never happen. Pair each safety property with a cover property for the state
that triggers it, and treat an unreachable cover as a failure of the property set: either an assumption over-constrains the
design or the trigger is wrong. A green proof with a failed cover proves nothing.

## Reset and the first cycle
Properties about the previous cycle are meaningless in the first cycle after reset. The compiler guards for that; if you ever
write a property by hand, gate every `$past()` use with a register that is 0 in the first cycle and 1 afterwards.

## Reading a failed proof
The counterexample trace gives the failing property, the cycle, and the input values that lead to it. Find the signal named in
the failing property, follow its cone of influence in the RTL (the registers and inputs that can change it), and fix that
logic. Do not weaken the property to make it pass unless the property is what is wrong.

## Bounded versus unbounded
`bmc` finding no failure within N cycles only shows that no bug appears that early. `prove` with k-induction can show a
property holds forever, but needs the property to be inductive; if induction fails with a counterexample that starts from an
unreachable state, strengthen the property set with an invariant that rules the state out, not with an assumption that
changes the design's behaviour.

## Equivalence after synthesis
After synthesis the gate netlist must be equivalent to the RTL: build a miter of the two (`equiv_make gold gate equiv`), try
`equiv_simple`, then `equiv_induct`, and require `equiv_status -assert`. A design with module instances must be flattened
before the equivalence passes can run on it.
name: sva_formal_patterns

content:
# Verilator lint messages and how to fix them

Verilator is run with `--lint-only -Wall`. An `%Error` stops the flow; a `%Warning-NAME` is reported and counted. The fix for
each common message is below. Change only the lines the message names.

## WIDTH WIDTHTRUNC WIDTHEXPAND width mismatch
The two sides of an assignment or operator have different bit widths (for example an 8-bit expression assigned to a 4-bit
signal, or a 32-bit `integer` added to a 4-bit counter). Make the widths agree: size literals (`4'd1`, not `1`), slice
deliberately (`sum[3:0]`), or zero-extend with a concatenation (`{4'd0, nibble}`). Do not silence the warning with a pragma
when the truncation is a real bug.

## UNUSEDSIGNAL UNUSEDPARAM unused signal or parameter
A signal or parameter is declared and never read. It is a warning, not an error. Delete it, or use it. Unused input bits that
belong to a fixed port list are fine; do not change the ports to remove the warning.

## UNDRIVEN UNASSIGNED signal never assigned
A signal is read but nothing drives it, or a vector has bits nothing drives. Assign it in a combinational block or with
`assign`, or remove it. An undriven output port is always a bug.

## CASEINCOMPLETE case statement without default
A `case` does not cover every value and has no `default`. Add `default:` that assigns every signal the block drives. In a
combinational block this also prevents an inferred latch.

## LATCH inferred latch combinational block does not assign on every path
In `always_comb`, a signal is assigned under an `if` but not in the `else`, or in some `case` arms only. Put a default
assignment for every driven signal at the top of the block (`y = 1'b0;`) and then override it, or complete every branch.

## BLKSEQ blocking assignment in a sequential block
Inside `always_ff @(posedge clk)` use non-blocking assignment `<=` for registers. A blocking `=` there is reported by
Verilator (BLKSEQ) and by SiliconForge as `SF-RTL-004`.

## COMBDLY non-blocking assignment in a combinational block
Inside `always_comb` or `always @*` use blocking assignment `=`. A non-blocking `<=` that is a real assignment there is
reported as COMBDLY and as `SF-RTL-005`. A `<=` that is a less-or-equal comparison (`if (count <= LIMIT)`) is not an
assignment and is fine.

## MULTIDRIVEN signal driven from more than one block
Two `always` blocks, or an `assign` and an `always`, drive the same signal. Each signal must have exactly one driver: move
all assignments to one block, or split the signal into two.

## UNOPTFLAT combinational loop
The path printed under "Example path" is a loop through combinational logic, often because a vector is both read and
written in one `always_comb`. Break the loop with a register, or split the vector into separate signals so that each bit
depends only on earlier ones. A genuine combinational loop is never intended in synchronous RTL.

## Can't find definition of variable undeclared signal
A name is used and never declared, typically a temporary inside `always_comb` (`next_state`, `next_count`). Declare it before
use at module scope: `logic [3:0] next_count;`. The error line shows the first use.

## syntax error unexpected '=' statement outside a block
A line such as `ready_o = valid_reg;` sits at module level, where only declarations, `assign`, instances and `always` blocks
are allowed. Write `assign ready_o = valid_reg;` for continuous logic, or move the statement inside an `always_comb` block.

## syntax error expecting reserved word as an identifier
A signal is named with a keyword (`input`, `output`, `reg`, `wire`, `logic`, `type`, `bit`, `do`, `default`). Rename it, for
example `data_in`, `reg_q`.

## SiliconForge static lint rules SF-RTL
SF-RTL-001: a `#delay` was found; delays are not synthesizable, remove them. SF-RTL-002: an `initial` block outside
`` `ifdef FORMAL ``; use the reset instead. SF-RTL-003: a `$display`-style task in RTL (warning). SF-RTL-004: blocking `=` in
`always_ff`. SF-RTL-005: non-blocking `<=` assignment in `always_comb`. SF-RTL-006: possible latch, an `if` without `else`
in `always_comb` (warning).
name: verilator_warnings
